title: Electric Circuits
seo_title: Grade 6 Natural Sciences and Technology: Electric Circuits Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 6 Natural Sciences and Technology: Electric circuits; conductors and insulators; mains electricity
standard_text: An electric circuit needs a source of energy (cell), conductors (wires) and a load (bulb) in a complete loop; switches open and close the circuit. Conductors let electricity flow; insulators do not. Mains electricity is dangerous and must be used safely; illegal connections are dangerous. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences and Technology, Grade 6, Energy and Change: Electric circuits; conductors and insulators; mains electricity)

body_html:
How to think about it

A circuit has a cell (energy source), wires (conductors) and a bulb, buzzer or motor (load) joined in a complete loop. A switch opens the circuit (off) and closes it (on). Circuits are drawn with symbols.

Metals such as copper are conductors; plastic, rubber, wood and glass are insulators. Mains electricity from the wall is much stronger than a cell and can kill. Never touch plugs with wet hands, never overload plugs and stay away from illegal connections and fallen power lines.

Example

A paper clip is put in a gap in a circuit and the bulb lights. Is it a conductor?

Electricity flows through it.

Answer: yes

Example

What happens when a switch is opened?

The loop is broken.

Answer: the bulb goes off

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a bulb lights with one wire to the cell.
  • Thinking water is a safe insulator.
  • Thinking mains electricity is as safe as a torch cell.

No, because it is an insulator.

items.q: A lamp in a circuit will not light. Two cells are both facing the same way, but the lamp still will not light. One cell is very old. What is the most likely reason?
c: Six lamps share the voltage of one cell, so each gets very little.
One cell is flat, so there is not enough voltage.
Plastic is an insulator, so it blocks the current.
The old cell had run out.
items.e: Check: cells, bulb, every connection, switches and materials.

items.q: Will the bulb light?
c: Yes, but only for a second.
Yes. Most of the wires are connected.
No. A wire is not connected, so the circuit is open.
items.e: Every part of the loop must be connected for current to flow.

items.q: Will the motor spin?
c: Yes. The circuit is closed, so current flows all the way around.
items.e: The path goes from the battery, through the motor and back with no gaps.

items.q: An electric kettle of power 2 kW is used for 5 hours. Electricity costs 35 cents per kWh. What is the cost?
